candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Make fractional parts directly comparable before subtraction by finding a common denominator, rewriting equivalent fractions, or expressing a whole number as a whole plus 0 over the needed denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe the same preparation skill of making fractional parts comparable via common denominators/equivalent fractions; A and C explicitly include rewriting a whole number as 0 over a denominator, while B includes that only when tied to alignment.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a mixed number with an improper fractional part as an equivalent standard mixed number before subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A and C match exactly on normalizing improper mixed-number forms; B includes this same concept but also broadens the skill to include rewriting whole numbers as whole plus 0 over a denominator, so B.S02 spans this concept plus part of alignment/preparation.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Carry out subtraction once quantities are in compatible form by subtracting numerators of like fractions and subtracting whole and fractional parts of mixed numbers directly.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts identify the core execution skill of subtracting after setup is complete. A restricts it to no-borrowing cases, while B and C define the same direct subtraction operation more generally but exclude regrouping.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: When direct subtraction is not yet in final form, borrow 1 from the whole part to continue fractional subtraction and/or simplify the resulting fraction or zero form to lowest terms.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts combine borrowing/regrouping with final simplification into one skill. The wording differs slightly, but each includes borrowing from the whole part and simplifying the resulting fraction or zero form.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks are highly aligned, with four shared skill concepts appearing across all experts. The main difference is granularity: Expert B's Normalize mixed forms (S02) is broader than A and C's Normalize mixed numbers because it also includes rewriting whole numbers as whole plus 0 over a denominator, which overlaps with the alignment skill. Otherwise, the codebooks show near one-to-one correspondence across preparation, normalization, direct subtraction, and regrouping/simplification.
